inventory_reason: Six numbered substantive provisions. Paragraph 2 includes both status acquisition and reinstatement; paragraph 4 includes both notice and return arrangements; paragraph 6 includes both implementing authority and State-concurrence protection. Paragraph 7 supplies common activation, not a seventh continuing command. Titles, signature and contents are excluded.
chronology_reasoning: Partial candidate. The complete original establishes six continuing substantive rules, expressly effective as of September 1, 1947, although signed February 27, 1948. Individual four-year appointment eligibility, two-month notice, thirty-day reinstatement and waiver conditions do not set a whole-order calendar sunset. EO12107 expressly substitutes OPM for CSC effective January 1, 1979. EO12292 expressly revokes EO9932 effective February 15, 1981, rather than its February 23 signature date. That establishes termination by the cutoff but does not establish first cessation. The revoker identifies a concrete statutory transition from the incorporated 1946 reinstatement regime to 1980 Act section 310; actual statutory history and continuity are unread. Earlier actual Civil Service Rule III and appointment-system changes also require resolution for the status routes. Named-function searches additionally found narrower overseas-program reinstatement limitations; they are recorded as bounded leads and do not establish a global ending. Accrued competitive status and individual reinstatement rights are not declared invalid. Final search and savings closure are withheld, and provisional no status is unchanged.
1950 appointment conversions and EO10577 rules replacement are actual earlier leads, not assumed exhaustion of every original assignment/status case.
The 1959 and later overseas-program limits have express population qualifications and agency-agreement exceptions; no global date is inferred from an individual duration limit.
savings_reasoning: Original paragraph 6 protects already assigned personnel against later rule changes absent State concurrence. Original accrued competitive status and reinstatement outcomes are distinct from an ongoing rule. EO12107 section 2-202 has personnel-action savings, but EO9932 was amended, not revoked there; this provision is not treated as perpetual survival after EO12292. EO12292 contains no express target-specific savings; actual statutory transition remains unread. Therefore savings_residuals stays null.

quoted_parts:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, including the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (94 Stat. 
2071; 22 U.S.C. 3901 et seq .), and in order to conform existing Executive Orders 
to changes resulting from that Act, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Sec. 5. Executive Order No. 11034 is amended by striking out in Section 5(c) 
after “provided by section” all that follows in that sentence and inserting in 
lieu thereof “310 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3950).”.

(b) Section 1-401 is amended by striking out “528 of the Foreign Service Act of 
1946 (22 U.S.C. 928)” and inserting in lieu thereof, “310 of the Foreign Service 
Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3950)”.

(d) Section l-602(b) is amended by striking out “section 528 of the Foreign 
Service Act of 1946” and inserting in lieu thereof “section 310 of the Foreign 
Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3950)”.

gaps.needed: Read actual operative sections and material amendments, the 1980 replacement/repeal/effective and savings provisions, and determine their effect on each original command and accrued rights. No earlier cessation is inferred from the gap.

gaps.needed: Resolve the effect of those actual changes on pending versus already-acquired status, including implementing rules, without assuming that a changed appointment label or a closed appointment cohort proves exhaustion of all original duties.
